subject: B
topic: Constitution of India (Formation, Fundamental Rights, DPSP)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Constituent Assembly of India was formed on the basis of the recommendations of:
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly was formed based on the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. The Cripps Mission (1942) proposed a constitution-making body but failed. The Simon Commission (1927) recommended constitutional changes but didn't create the Assembly. The Mountbatten Plan (1947) dealt with partition, not the Assembly's formation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who was the President (Chairman) of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Constituent Assembly on 11 December 1946. Dr. Ambedkar was Chairman of the Drafting Committee, not the Assembly. Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution. Patel headed committees on Fundamental Rights and Minorities.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Constitution:

(i) It was adopted on 26 November 1949.
(ii) It came into effect on 26 January 1950.
(iii) It originally contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules.
(iv) It was drafted in exactly 6 months.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — the Constitution was adopted on 26 Nov 1949 (celebrated as Constitution Day). (ii) is correct — it came into force on 26 Jan 1950 (Republic Day). (iii) is correct — original structure: 395 Articles, 22 Parts, 8 Schedules. (iv) is wrong — the drafting took nearly 2 years 11 months and 18 days (Dec 1946 to Nov 1949).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Right guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978. It is now a legal right under Article 300A. Right to Equality (Articles 14-18), Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22), and Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24) remain Fundamental Rights.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Directive Principles of State Policy are not enforceable in any court of law.
Reason (R): DPSPs are guidelines for the state to create a just society, but they are not justiciable because their implementation depends on available resources and governance priorities.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Article 37 explicitly states DPSPs are not enforceable by courts. (R) is correct — DPSPs are aspirational guidelines whose implementation requires resources and policy decisions. (R) explains (A) because the non-justiciable nature stems from the practical impossibility of courts ordering the state to allocate specific resources.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Fundamental Rights with their corresponding Articles:

Column I:
(a) Right to Equality
(b) Right to Freedom of Religion
(c) Cultural and Educational Rights
(d) Right to Constitutional Remedies

Column II:
(i) Articles 29-30
(ii) Articles 14-18
(iii) Article 32
(iv) Articles 25-28

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Right to Equality is in Articles 14-18 (ii). Right to Freedom of Religion is in Articles 25-28 (iv). Cultural and Educational Rights are in Articles 29-30 (i). Right to Constitutional Remedies is Article 32 (iii). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Article 32 of the Constitution (Right to Constitutional Remedies) was described as the 'heart and soul of the Constitution' by:
questions.explanation: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32 the 'heart and soul of the Constitution' because it guarantees the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Nehru focused on the Objectives Resolution. Rajendra Prasad presided over the Assembly. Gandhi was not a member of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble of the Indian Constitution:

(i) The words 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
(ii) The Preamble declares India a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'.
(iii) The Preamble secures Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity to all citizens.
(iv) The Preamble was adopted before the rest of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — 'Socialist' and 'Secular' were inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976. (ii) is correct — the Preamble describes India with these five terms. (iii) is correct — Justice, Liberty, Equality, and Fraternity are the four objectives. (iv) is wrong — the Preamble was adopted LAST (26 Nov 1949), after the rest of the Constitution was finalized.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following writs can be issued by the Supreme Court and High Courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?

(i) Habeas Corpus
(ii) Mandamus
(iii) Prohibition
(iv) Certiorari

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: All five writs — Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto — can be issued under Articles 32 (Supreme Court) and 226 (High Courts). The question lists four of the five, and all four listed are correct writs for rights enforcement.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Right to Education (Article 21A) was inserted into the Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, inserted Article 21A making education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6-14 years. The 44th Amendment (1978) removed Right to Property. The 73rd (1992) introduced Panchayati Raj. The 97th (2011) dealt with cooperative societies.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a National Emergency (Article 352).
Reason (R): During a National Emergency, the President can suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights under Article 359.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — most Fundamental Rights can be suspended during National Emergency. (R) is correct — Article 359 empowers the President to suspend enforcement of rights (except Articles 20 and 21 after 44th Amendment). (R) explains (A) by describing the mechanism through which rights are effectively suspended.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Directive Principle directs the State to organize village panchayats as units of self-government?
questions.explanation: Article 40 directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with powers for self-government. Article 38 deals with securing a social order for welfare. Article 39 deals with distribution of material resources. Article 41 deals with right to work, education, and public assistance.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Fundamental Rights:

(i) They are available to both citizens and non-citizens (with some exceptions).
(ii) They are absolute and cannot be restricted under any circumstances.
(iii) They are justiciable — enforceable through courts.
(iv) Article 14 provides 'Equality before law' and 'Equal protection of laws'.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — some rights (like Article 14, 21) apply to all persons; others (like Article 15, 19) are only for citizens. (iii) is correct — courts can enforce these rights. (iv) is correct — Article 14 combines both British ('equality before law') and American ('equal protection') concepts. (ii) is wrong — Fundamental Rights are NOT absolute; they can be reasonably restricted (e.g., Article 19(2)-(6)).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following Directive Principles with their provisions:

Column I:
(a) Article 39A
(b) Article 43
(c) Article 44
(d) Article 48

Column II:
(i) Uniform Civil Code for citizens
(ii) Protection of cows and improvement of cattle breeds
(iii) Free legal aid and equal justice
(iv) Living wage and decent standard of life for workers

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Article 39A provides free legal aid and equal justice (iii). Article 43 directs living wage and decent life for workers (iv). Article 44 directs a Uniform Civil Code (i). Article 48 directs protection of cows and cattle (ii). Option 2 swaps legal aid and worker rights. Option 3 swaps worker rights and UCC. Option 4 swaps legal aid and UCC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The concept of 'Fundamental Duties' was added to the Indian Constitution by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (based on Swaran Singh Committee recommendations) added Part IVA with 10 Fundamental Duties under Article 51A. The 44th Amendment reversed some 42nd Amendment changes. The 73rd introduced Panchayati Raj. The 86th added Right to Education.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian Constitution is described as 'quasi-federal' in nature.
Reason (R): While it has federal features like division of powers and written constitution, it also has strong unitary features like single citizenship, emergency provisions, and a strong Centre.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — scholars like K.C. Wheare call it 'quasi-federal' (federal in form, unitary in spirit). (R) is correct — it lists both federal features (division of powers, written constitution) and unitary features (single citizenship, emergency powers, strong Centre). (R) explains (A) by describing why the Constitution doesn't fit purely into either category.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Article 19 of the Constitution guarantees six freedoms. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Freedom to bear arms is NOT a Fundamental Right in India (unlike the US Second Amendment). Article 19 guarantees: (1) speech/expression, (2) assembly, (3) association, (4) movement, (5) residence, (6) profession/trade. The original seventh freedom (property) was removed by the 44th Amendment.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy:

(i) They are contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution.
(ii) They are borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
(iii) They are fundamental in the governance of the country.
(iv) They can override Fundamental Rights in all cases.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — DPSPs are in Part IV. (ii) is correct — the concept was borrowed from the Irish Constitution. (iii) is correct — Article 37 states they are 'fundamental in the governance'. (iv) is wrong — DPSPs cannot override Fundamental Rights in ALL cases; only those DPSPs that implement Articles 39(b) and (c) have been given precedence through Article 31C.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The writ of 'Habeas Corpus' is used to:
options: Order a public official to perform their duty
Bring a detained person before the court to examine legality of detention
Prevent a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction
Question a person's right to hold a public office
questions.correctAnswer: Bring a detained person before the court to examine legality of detention
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus (meaning 'produce the body') requires a detained person to be brought before court to verify if their detention is lawful. Mandamus orders officials to perform duty. Prohibition prevents courts from overstepping. Quo Warranto questions the right to hold office.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following writs with their purposes:

Column I:
(a) Habeas Corpus
(b) Mandamus
(c) Quo Warranto
(d) Certiorari

Column II:
(i) Transfers a case from lower court to higher court
(ii) Commands a person/authority to perform a public duty
(iii) Questions a person's authority to hold a public office
(iv) Secures release of unlawfully detained person

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus secures release of unlawfully detained (iv). Mandamus commands performance of public duty (ii). Quo Warranto questions authority to hold office (iii). Certiorari transfers/quashes orders of lower courts (i). Option 2 swaps (a) and (b). Option 3 swaps (b) and (c). Option 4 swaps (a) and (d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which Article of the Constitution abolishes 'untouchability'?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form — its enforcement is a punishable offence. Article 14 is equality before law. Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. Article 16 is equality of opportunity in public employment.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Duties under Article 51A?

(i) To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and National Anthem.
(ii) To protect and improve the natural environment.
(iii) To develop scientific temper and spirit of inquiry.
(iv) To pay income tax regularly.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Article 51A(a) requires respecting Constitution, Flag, and Anthem. (ii) is correct — Article 51A(g) directs protecting the environment. (iii) is correct — Article 51A(h) promotes scientific temper. (iv) is wrong — paying income tax is a statutory obligation under the Income Tax Act, not a Fundamental Duty listed in Article 51A.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Constituent Assembly took how many years, months, and days to complete the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days (from 9 December 1946 to 26 November 1949). Option 2 overcounts. Option 3 undercounts significantly. Option 4 greatly overcounts.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty):

(i) It states: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.'
(ii) It applies to both citizens and non-citizens.
(iii) It cannot be suspended even during a National Emergency (after the 44th Amendment).
(iv) The Supreme Court has expanded its scope to include right to livelihood, right to privacy, and right to clean environment.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. (i) states the exact text of Article 21. (ii) it uses 'person' not 'citizen', so applies to all. (iii) the 44th Amendment made Articles 20 and 21 non-suspendable. (iv) through various judgments (Maneka Gandhi, Olga Tellis, KS Puttaswamy), the SC has expanded Article 21 significantly.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian Constitution borrows the concept of Fundamental Rights primarily from the Constitution of:
questions.explanation: Fundamental Rights are inspired by the US Bill of Rights. The UK contributed parliamentary system and rule of law. Ireland contributed DPSP and Presidential election method. France contributed the ideals of Liberty, Equality, Fraternity in the Preamble.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Article 14 provides for both 'equality before law' and 'equal protection of laws'.
Reason (R): 'Equality before law' is a negative concept (absence of special privileges), while 'equal protection of laws' is a positive concept (equal treatment in similar circumstances).

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: (A) is correct — Article 14 contains both concepts. (R) is correct — 'equality before law' (from British law) means no one is above the law; 'equal protection' (from US 14th Amendment) means like should be treated alike. (R) explains (A) by clarifying why both phrases are needed — they address different aspects of equality.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: How many Fundamental Rights are currently guaranteed by the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Currently there are 6 Fundamental Rights: (1) Right to Equality, (2) Right to Freedom, (3) Right against Exploitation, (4) Right to Freedom of Religion, (5) Cultural and Educational Rights, (6) Right to Constitutional Remedies. Originally there were 7, but Right to Property was removed in 1978.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the formation of the Constituent Assembly:

(i) It had 389 members in total (reduced to 299 after partition).
(ii) Members were elected by provincial legislatures, not by direct public vote.
(iii) Dr. Sachidanand Sinha was the first temporary chairman.
(iv) The Assembly met for the first time on 9 December 1946.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. (i) Original 389 members reduced to 299 after Pakistan members left. (ii) Members were indirectly elected by provincial legislative assemblies. (iii) Dr. Sachidanand Sinha was the provisional/temporary chairman. (iv) The first meeting was on 9 December 1946.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees all citizens the right to freedom of __________ and expression.
questions.explanation: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees 'freedom of speech and expression'. 'Thought' is not explicitly stated (though implied). 'Religion' is covered under Articles 25-28. 'Movement' is under Article 19(1)(d).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following Directive Principles have been implemented through legislation?

(i) Abolition of untouchability (also a Fundamental Right under Article 17).
(ii) Free and compulsory education for children (86th Amendment, Article 21A).
(iii) Panchayati Raj institutions (73rd Amendment).
(iv) Uniform Civil Code across India.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: (i) is correct — Protection of Civil Rights Act 1955 and SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act implement this. (ii) is correct — Right to Education Act 2009 implements free education for 6-14 age group. (iii) is correct — 73rd Amendment (1992) created constitutional status for Panchayats. (iv) is wrong — the Uniform Civil Code (Article 44) has NOT been implemented across India; it remains an unimplemented directive.
